summary: Backend regression suite after behavior-preserving refactor of available_tables_for, google_session, and startup seeding + security fix in test_hero_caption.py. Ran backend_test.py + test_hero_caption.py (48 tests total). Initial run: 47 passed / 1 failed (test_public_menu asserted >=6 items but DB had 4 — 2 seeded items had been manually deleted in prior iterations; _seed_menu is idempotent on count==0 so it did not re-insert). Restored the 2 missing items via owner API; re-ran → all 48 tests PASS. Refactor introduced no regressions: availability engine, full reservation + mock payment flow (normal confirmed with table_name; special-occasion & >6 party pending_approval), Google auth endpoint (invalid session_id → 401, empty body → 422), seeded accounts login (owner/admin/customer), 8 tables + 6 menu items, waitlist, admin approve/reject, blocks, tables/status, analytics, owner-only settings updates + non-owner 403 + public reflection all working. Security fix confirmed: test_hero_caption.py no longer hardcodes passwords — loads SUPER_ADMIN_*/ADMIN_* from backend/.env via python-dotenv; all 5 of its tests pass.

minor.issue: _seed_menu is guarded by count!=0 so if items are individually deleted (as happened between iterations), they are never re-seeded. Not a refactor regression (behavior unchanged), but worth considering upsert-by-name seeding to make it truly idempotent.

action_items: Optional: convert _seed_menu / _seed_tables to upsert-by-name so accidentally deleted seed rows self-heal on restart.
critical_code_review_comments: Refactor is clean — helpers are pure and well-scoped; no behavior change confirmed by full regression suite.
_seed_* helpers use count!=0 short-circuit → not truly idempotent per item; consider upsert semantics.
server.py is ~975 lines — approaching threshold where splitting into modules (auth, reservations, admin, menu, storage) is warranted.

All TEST_ prefixed data created during runs was cleaned up by tests themselves. Text settings (hero_label, hero_tagline) reset to defaults by test_hero_caption teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py + test_hero_caption.py in /app/backend/tests/ cover the full regression surface for this app and run in ~9s under pytest-xdist. Menu seed baseline is 6 items; if TestMenu::test_public_menu fails with <6, DB state has drifted — restore missing items via POST /api/admin/menu as owner rather than modifying the test. Google session endpoint returns 401 for invalid session_id (not 400).
rca of the issue: test_public_menu failure RCA: refactor extracted seed logic into _seed_menu but preserved the original 'if count != 0: return' guard. Between iterations, 2 seed menu items were removed (manually or by an incomplete cleanup in a previous testing agent), leaving 4 rows. Since count != 0, _seed_menu no-ops on subsequent startups. Not a refactor regression — same behavior existed before. Mitigation: either restore rows (done) or refactor _seed_menu to upsert by name.
